nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Quantile regression was used to determine percentile curves (5th, 50th, 95th) for each cortical region and white matter tract. The model included age, sex, age-squared (when justified by BIC), sex-by-age interaction (when justified by BIC), and site as nuisance confounds. Bootstrapping was used to estimate confidence intervals for each percentile.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Quantile regression [35, 36] was used to determine percentile curves for each cortical region and each white matter tract. Whereas conventional regression aims to predict the mean of a response variable (e.g., CT or FA), given certain explanatory variables (e.g., age and sex), quantile regression aims to predict percentiles of interest, such as the median (50th percentile). This enabled statistical operationalization of a normative range of variation in terms of percentiles expressed as a function of age and sex.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Fractional anisotropy (FA) was measured for 48 white matter tracts (ICBM-DTI-81 atlas) and cortical thickness (CT) was measured for 68 cortical regions (Desikan-Killiany atlas). FA images were computed from diffusion-weighted MRI using FSL and tract-averaged. CT was estimated using FreeSurfer 6.0 and region-averaged.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Cortical thickness (CT) was measured to index changes in gray matter comprising the cortical sheet, while fractional anisotropy (FA) provided a broad measure of axonal health in white matter.; FA was averaged overall voxels comprising each of the 48 white matter tracts delineated within the ICBM-DTI-81 white matter atlas. Hence, each individual was characterized by a tract-averaged FA value for each of 48 distinct white matter tracts.; Cortical thickness was averaged overall vertices comprising each of the 68 cortical regions of the Desikan-Killiany atlas.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and sex with optional age-squared and sex-by-age interaction terms; acquisition site included as a confound.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: given certain explanatory variables (e.g., age and sex) ... Ci encapsulates nuisance confounds, including acquisition site. The sex-by-age interaction (β3) and the nonlinear age-squared term (β4) were only included when justified by the Bayesian information criteria.
